h: Joy in the Holiness Given Beyond Our Awareness

p: as corresponding to the seven shepherds,
who correspond to the seven middos;
and it lists the Shabbos Mussaf
the middah of Tzaddik Yesod Olam.
For the additional holiness of Shabbos
corresponds to the middah of Yesod,
for Shabbos is in the secret of the covenant,
as is found in the holy Zohar (in several places).
And in the holy Zohar (end of Parashas Balak):
"The Tzaddik is called sasson, joy," etc.;
"'And you shall draw water with joy' (Yeshayahu 12:3):
"And you shall draw water with joy":
Chochmah alludes to the Written Torah
and Binah to Torah she'b'al peh,
in the name of the Yerushalmi)
it expounds "And you shall draw water with joy":
"that from there they draw ruach hakodesh," etc.
is the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ן (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יב, א)
that "a sage is superior to a prophet":
for a great man says something,
and a halachah l'Moshe mi'Sinai is stated
and he aims at "the word of Hashem,"
which is the words of the living God;
And it is the aspect of Daas,
as it says in Rashi (Parashas Ki Sisa, Shemos 31:3):
"'And with knowledge': this is ruach hakodesh";
and it is the inwardness from Kesser Elyon,
and it comes through the joining
and this is "with joy, from the wellsprings of salvation."
And that is why it says,
בְּסִיּוּם הַפְטוֹרָה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (יְשַׁעְיָה נא, ג)
at the close of this parashah's haftarah (Yeshayahu 51:3):
"Joy and gladness will be found in her."
And it is found in the holy Zohar (Balak, ibid.):
כִּי בְשִׂמְחָה תֵצֵאוּ (יְשַׁעְיָה נה, יב) וְכוּלֵּי
"'For with joy you will go out' (Yeshayahu 55:12)," etc.,
"the Shechinah goes out with them," etc.
And that is why it says (ibid. 51:3):
He has comforted all her ruins,
and He has made her wilderness like Eden
and her desert like the garden of Hashem";
And so it appears from the wording of the pasuk
which is an entirely desolate place,
one must make the way of Hashem.
שֶׁהוּא מָקוֹם שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ יִשּׁוּב וְדֶרֶךְ
being a place that had habitation and a road,
and so it has in it
one need only straighten what is crooked;
and this is "Make straight in the desert."
And mesillah means a trodden path,
אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם עוֹז לוֹ בָךְ (תְּהִלִּים פד, ו)
"'Fortunate is the man whose strength is in You' (Tehillim 84:6):
For the paths of the Torah
where there was already a road,
all that is lacking is to straighten it
and this is "a highway for our God."
"Your holy cities have become a wilderness;
that it seems like a wilderness,
as if there had never been habitation.
He has comforted all her ruins":
these are Yerushalayim and "Your holy cities";
which is like a place desolate forever,
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת לד, ב)
over which there has not ruled
and the holy Zohar calls Eden
the aspect of the intellect hidden
That is, Hashem Yisbarach will make clear
that they were bound at the root,
"And her desert like the garden of Hashem,"
"And a river goes out from Eden
which is the souls of Knesses Yisrael;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ
as the holy Zohar on this parashah writes
that they are the secret of oneg, "delight,"
the initials of Eden, Nahar, Gan.
"will be found," in the sense of a find,
along the lines of what it says (Shabbos 130a):
And from where is it implied
And the mitzvah of milah on the eighth day,
when the infant as yet knows nothing at all,
but is circumcised by his parents,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א צג, א)
as written in the holy Zohar (I 93a),
"And your people, all of them righteous"
which is the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh;
which is not seen as it comes down,
רַק מִמַּה שֶּׁאָנוּ רוֹאִין אַחַר כָּךְ
but only from what we see afterward,
is it evident that dew came down.
So too with Torah she'b'al peh:
that he is innovating the words of Torah,
but in truth they are the words of the living God,
which Hashem Yisbarach shines into him,
"'The word of Hashem': this is halachah."
So too milah on the eighth day,
And this is "And you shall draw water,"
that is, the words of Torah,
So too according to the exposition of the Yerushalmi cited above,
that from there they draw ruach hakodesh,
that is, Torah she'b'al peh, as stated,
which is the aspect of Daas,
and in the holy Zohar it is called
and this is "And a river goes out from Eden
And this is what the pasuk says (Mishlei 4:22):
"They are life to those who find them":
for the words of Torah are also
that he innovates by himself, with his own intellect;
and this is "Joy and gladness will be found in her."
according to what is written in the Tosefta
Go and offer a bull on my behalf," etc.
Father, why did you see fit
to rejoice in the joy of this mitzvah
All the mitzvos in the Torah
נָתַן לָנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְדַעְתֵּינוּ
HaKadosh Baruch Hu gave us to perform knowingly;
this one, without our knowledge," etc.
So too the thanksgiving offering comes
that Hashem Yisbarach sends to a person
and this is "thanksgiving and the sound of song,"
And regarding Shabbos it is found
the Torah was given on Shabbos.
is in the secret of the covenant,
"For I am Hashem Who sanctifies you."
Therefore the additional holiness of Shabbos
is counted in the holy Zohar
as corresponding to the middah of Yosef HaTzaddik;
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem
and to sing to Your Name, O Most High."
